prs.title: Editorial: Don't mention writability in the Global Environment Record GetBindingValue description
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
GetBindingValue does not care about writability (as you can confirm by reading the algorithm and seeing that it will bottom out in [GetBindingValue for Object environment records](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#sec-object-environment-records-getbindingvalue-n-s)). Presumably this was copied from the SetMutableBinding section above it when this section was introduced in ES2015.

Cherry-pick of the commit from #4012 by @JinDX.

prs.title: Editorial: qualify claim about TA length changing during sort
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
This note became incorrect with the introduction of resizable ArrayBuffers, though arguably it was already incorrect given ArrayBuffer detaching. As reported in #4013 by @JinDX.

I think the "no user code" note is useful; the `UC` annotation doesn't suffice because it will tell you that SortIndexedProperties can call user code - which it can, but only by calling the user-provided comparator. That really can change the length of the TA during execution although the algorithm mostly doesn't care (it does all the reads before calling the comparator, and the trailing writes just don't happen if the TA ends up too small for them).

I'm open to dropping the "and the TypedArray's length cannot decrease" part since it's a little confusing in light of the up-front read.

prs.title: Editorial: clarify hyperbolic function identities
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from #4015 by @JinDX.

These notes are incorrect as written. They presumably aren't intended to be binding constraints on the "implementation-approximated Number value", and in any case they aren't in practice. But it's still useful to explain to a reader what these functions are.

prs.title: Editorial: correct the Date.parse expression count
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from #4017 by @JinDX.

This actually [goes back to ES5](https://es5.github.io/#x10.2.1), which introduced `toISOString` and therefore increased the number of expressions. In [ES3](https://www-archive.mozilla.org/js/language/e262-3.pdf) there really were only three.

prs.title: Editorial: add missing coercion in HostGrowSharedArrayBuffer description
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from #4024 by @JinDX.

HostGrowSharedArrayBuffer takes a (mathematical) non-negative integer, and then the prose requirements require in some case  an event whose "[[Payload]] is NumericToRawBytes(`~biguint64~`, `_newByteLength_`, `_isLittleEndian_`)". But the second argument to NumericToRawBytes must be a Number or BigInt, so coerce with `ℤ`.

prs.title: Editorial: Fix the target field name in the FinalizationRegistry register note
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from https://github.com/tc39/ecma262/pull/4026 by @JinDX.

Incidentally this should maybe be a named Record type, but that can be done separately. There's actually [a note](https://tc39.es/ecma262/multipage/executable-code-and-execution-contexts.html#sec-liveness) (note 5) that refers to these as "a FinalizationRegistry Cell record" already.

prs.title: Editorial: fix Annex B CompileAssertion substitution names
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from #4027 by @JinDX.

I assume this was a copy/paste error from the CompileSubpattern section above, which really does substitute |QuantifiableAssertion| for |Atom|.

prs.title: Editorial: fix bound function name in bind note
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from #4028 by @JinDX.

#3789 renamed both the alias in the algorithm and in the note (from `_F_`), but to different names.

prs.title: Editorial: describe the decodeURI preserve set accurately
prs.author: bakkot
prs.body:
Cherry-pick of the commit from #4029 by @JinDX.

The current description is incorrect: `encodeURI` cannot introduce the escape sequence `%41`, but `decodeURI('%41')` does decode it (to `"A"`).

This has actually been wrong since ES3, when these algorithms and this prose was introduced.

prs.title: Editorial: clarify the return value of Atomics.waitAsync
prs.author: JinDX
prs.body:
This replaces #4002. I accidentally deleted and recreated my fork, which closed the original PR and prevents it from being reopened. This PR restores its final patch, including the wording suggested during review.

The introductory paragraph of `Atomics.waitAsync` currently describes its return value as a Promise.

Update it to match the `DoWait` algorithm: the method returns an object with `async` and `value` properties. When `async` is `true`, `value` is a Promise; otherwise, `value` is either `"not-equal"` or `"timed-out"`.

This is an editorial clarification; the algorithm is unchanged.

I have translated the entire ECMAScript specification into [Chinese](https://ecma262.com/c/), [Japanese](https://ecma262.com/j/), and [Korean](https://ecma262.com/k/) on ecma262.com. I noticed this discrepancy while reviewing these translations.

prs.title: Editorial: Refactor InLeapYear to move float math into callers
prs.author: ptomato
prs.body:
This moves the YearFromTime step (which does floating-point math on the passed time value) out of InLeapYear and into its callers, so that InLeapYear is now purely a series of modulo operations on an integer.

Also make the return type a Boolean which is the logical choice for an AO that is a predicate.

The motivation for this is because "is this integer year a leap year or not" is an operation needed in Temporal and it would be convenient not to have to worry about floating-point math when using it.
